Novak Djokovic.text: He has spent a record 428 weeks as the world No. 1, and ten of his majors are Australian Opens.
Novak Djokovic.evidence: He has been ranked as the world No. 1 in men's singles by the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) for a record 428 weeks ... Djokovic has won 102 ATP Tour–level singles titles, including a record 24 majors (including a record ten Australian Open titles)

Margaret Court.text: She won all four majors in 1970, and in 1991 became a Christian minister.
Margaret Court.evidence: She completed the Grand Slam by winning all four major singles titles in 1970, part of a record six consecutive major singles victories. ... Having grown up Catholic, Court became associated with Pentecostalism in the 1970s and became a Christian minister in that tradition in 1991.

Serena Williams.text: She won her 23rd major, the 2017 Australian Open, while already pregnant.
Serena Williams.evidence: On April 19, 2017, Williams revealed that she was 20 weeks pregnant and would miss the remainder of the season. The timing of her announcement meant she was already pregnant when she won the Australian Open.

Rafael Nadal.text: 14 of his 22 majors came at one tournament: the French Open.
Rafael Nadal.evidence: Nadal won 92 ATP Tour singles titles, with 22 major titles—including a record 14 French Open titles—as well as 36 Masters titles and two Olympic gold medals.

Steffi Graf.text: In 1988 she won all four majors and Olympic gold, the first Golden Slam.
Steffi Graf.evidence: In 1988, Graf ascended to dominance, becoming the first tennis player to achieve the Golden Slam by winning all four major titles and the Olympic gold medal in the same calendar year.

Roger Federer.text: He was a ball boy at his hometown tournament in Basel; he went on to win a record eight Wimbledons.
Roger Federer.evidence: Federer was also a ball boy at his hometown Basel event, the Swiss Indoors in 1992 and 1993 ... including 20 major men's singles titles (among which a record eight men's singles Wimbledon titles

Helen Wills Moody.text: Her stony calm on court earned her the nickname "Little Miss Poker Face".
Helen Wills Moody.evidence: Because of her unchanging stoic expression, Grantland Rice, the American sportswriter, bestowed on Wills the nickname "Little Miss Poker Face".

Chris Evert.text: She won at least one major for 13 years in a row, a record.
Chris Evert.evidence: Evert holds the record of most consecutive years (13) of winning at least one major title, and contested an all-time record 34 major women's singles finals.

Martina Navratilova.text: Her nine Wimbledon singles titles are an all-time record.
Martina Navratilova.evidence: Her nine Wimbledon singles titles are an all-time record.

Pete Sampras.text: His 14 majors were the men's record when he retired; seven came at Wimbledon.
Pete Sampras.evidence: Sampras won 64 ATP Tour-level singles titles, including 14 men's singles majors, which was an all-time record at the time of his retirement: seven Wimbledon Championships, two Australian Opens and an Open Era joint-record five US Opens.
